narrative.summaryIntro:
Ramanathaswamy Temple in Rameswaram, Tamil Nadu, is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas and forms the terminal shrine of the Char Dham (four cardinal pilgrimage sites). Dedicated to Lord Shiva as Ramanathaswamy, the temple is situated at the southernmost tip of the Indian peninsula and holds immense significance in Hindu pilgrimage tradition. According to the Ramayana, Lord Rama visited this sacred site after his return from Lanka.

The temple is renowned for its magnificent Dravidian architecture and particularly for its corridors, which are said to be the longest in any Indian temple. The temple features elaborate stone pillars, intricate carvings, and sacred tanks. The site attracts millions of pilgrims annually, and the journey to Rameswaram is considered a sacred pilgrimage culmination point for devotees completing the Char Dham circuit.
